page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 virtual-CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning includes 600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, with no GPU hardware present.

Benchmark evaluations reveal solid multi-threaded performance balanced against lower single-thread execution efficiency. The processor registers bottom-quartile marks in single-threaded tests, including stress-ng (1285.68), Geekbench single-core (1132.0), single-threaded gzip compression (21.75 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (8.47 GB/sec). In parallel execution, the server reaches middle-tier scores, generating 13531.65 in stress-ng multi-core and 7072.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory throughput displays average results, yielding 754.5 GB/sec in small-block cached read tests and 88.17 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB reads. Redis SET throughput registers at 13.2 million operations per second, with static web serving achieving 11.91 GB/sec.

The bundled high-speed NVMe storage and balanced memory configuration offer qualitative efficiency by accommodating data-intensive intermediate tasks without requiring external disk attachments. A key performance tradeoff is the subdued per-core execution speed, making the system less suited for single-threaded processing. The instance profile aligns directly with relational and key-value databases requiring local scratch space, distributed caching, web serving, and general enterprise application hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.4xlarge is a general-purpose server offering 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, and 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPU accelerators, it maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate middle-tier multi-threaded throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 14384.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7072.0, balanced against lower single-thread execution speeds. The inclusion of bundled NVMe storage delivers qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding external volume fees for local temporary data and scratch space. This profile is engineered for distributed database layers, Redis caching, static web hosting, and general enterprise containerized workloads.
